cards.back: private, static and final methods — the compiler fixes the target
cards.extra: None of the three can be overridden, so the mapping cannot change at runtime. The call site and the code are decided at compile time.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.back: Every other method — ordinary instance methods that subclasses may override
cards.extra: They are virtual by default. The JVM looks up the implementation from the object's actual class at the call.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: Is overloading or overriding resolved at runtime?
cards.extra: Overload choice depends on the declared argument types, which are known when compiling — not on the objects involved.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: Why can a static method not be dynamically bound?
cards.back: Static methods are not inherited in the overriding sense — a subclass declaring the same signature hides it instead
cards.extra: There is no object to dispatch on, so the compiler binds the call to the declared type's version.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: Does static binding make a call faster?
cards.back: Marginally, because no runtime lookup is needed — but it is not the reason to choose a modifier
cards.extra: The JIT often removes the virtual lookup anyway through inlining. Design for semantics, not for this.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: If Animal a = new Dog() calls an overridden method, which version runs?
cards.back: Dog's — the variable's declared type does not decide, the object's runtime type does
cards.extra: That single sentence is dynamic binding. It is also why the declared type only restricts which methods are visible, not which body runs.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: What does the declared type of a reference control?
cards.back: Which members are visible to the compiler — not which implementation executes
cards.extra: Animal a = new Dog() cannot call Dog-only methods without a cast, yet Dog's overrides still run.
cards.source: baeldung.com — Static and Dynamic Binding in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding
